acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `ready_task` (`saffron/task.py:889`) rebuilds its reviews straight off
      the task's stored `findings.json` (`saffron/task.py:969`, assigned to
      `CellOutcome.reviews` at `saffron/task.py:1018`) and hardcodes the
      resumed outcome's `state` to `READY_FOR_REVIEW` (`saffron/task.py:1011`),
      never asking whether today's build still agrees. The ledger's own
      `READY_FOR_REVIEW` (checked at `saffron/task.py:911`) only ever meant
      whatever selection rule was live in `review.anchored_blockers`
      (`saffron/phases/review.py:787`) when REVIEW ran — the same rule
      `_disagreements` reads today when it renders the pull request body
      (`saffron/report/pr_body.py:327`) and the same rule REBUT's own
      blocker list is. So a `findings.json` written before `anchored_blockers`
      grew its `HOST_FILED` exemption can carry an unanchored survivor
      that today's build now selects as a blocker, with no `rebuttal.json`
      on disk because the task never reached REBUT under the rule that was
      live then (`saffron/task.py:976` reads `rebut_result` as `None` in
      exactly that case). `ready_task` now refuses that task by name instead
      of handing `package_ready_task` (`saffron/task.py:1027`, reached from
      `saffron package` at `saffron/cli.py:2510`) a `ReadyTask` whose
      `reviews` disagree with its own hardcoded state. A task whose stored
      blocker already reached a fresh `rebuttal.json` is untouched: a fresh
      REBUT answering it is exactly what let that cell reach
      `READY_FOR_REVIEW` in the first place, under whichever rule ran it.
    witness: tests/test_session.py::test_ready_task_refuses_a_stale_blocker_that_never_reached_rebut
    mutant:
      file: saffron/task.py
      find: "if rebut_result is None and (stale := anchored_blockers(reviews)):"
      replace: "if (stale := anchored_blockers(reviews)):"
    wrong_versions:
      - "The guard excludes every blocker whose claim starts with the host's `HOST_FILED` mark, the same way `LensReview.drop_rate` already does, so the one survivor this fix exists to catch is exactly the one it lets through unrefused."
      - "The guard tests `anchored_blockers(reviews)` for `is not None` instead of for truthiness, so a task whose stored findings carry no blocker at all is refused on every resumption."

---

## Context

Follow-up to **SA-0299** (`b-e40d09`), head `edc692f0`, which widened
`anchored_blockers` (`saffron/phases/review.py:787`) to select a
`HOST_FILED` survivor whether or not it anchors. That change touched
`saffron/phases/review.py`, `saffron/phases/rebut.py` and
`saffron/report/pr_body.py` — every *live* reader of a review's blocker
list. It never touched `saffron/task.py`, which was forbidden to it.

`saffron/task.py` holds a second, offline reader: `ready_task`
(`saffron/task.py:889`), reached from `package_ready_task`
(`saffron/task.py:1027`) by `saffron package`'s CLI handler
(`saffron/cli.py:2510`), for re-running PACKAGE on a task whose first
`package()` call raised. It rebuilds a `ReadyTask` from the ledger and the
task directory alone, with no live `CellOutcome`. It requires the ledger's
own row to already read `READY_FOR_REVIEW` (`saffron/task.py:911`) and
carry no pull request yet (`saffron/task.py:915`), then reads `reviews`
back off `findings.json` (`saffron/task.py:969`) and assembles them into a
fresh `CellOutcome` whose `state` it writes as the literal string
`"READY_FOR_REVIEW"` (`saffron/task.py:1011`), never re-deriving it.

That was safe before SA-0299, because the ledger's recorded
`READY_FOR_REVIEW` and `anchored_blockers`' own verdict on the same
`reviews` always agreed — both were decided by the one rule live at REVIEW
time, and no later build had moved the rule out from under old data.
SA-0299 moved it: a `findings.json` already on disk, carrying an unanchored
`HOST_FILED` survivor filed under the old rule, now reads as holding a
blocker under the new one, while the ledger's row still says
`READY_FOR_REVIEW` from before, and no `rebuttal.json` exists because the
task never reached REBUT. `ready_task` hands that mismatch straight to
`package_ready_task`, which calls `package_phase.package`, whose pull-request
body goes through `_disagreements` (`saffron/report/pr_body.py:327`,
reading `anchored_blockers` under today's rule): the survivor renders as a
numbered `Disagreements` row with no rebuttal and no verdict, since
`outcome.rebut_result` is `None`.

No existing test exercises this boundary: every test that builds
`findings.json` does so under the current build's own rule, so
`anchored_blockers` and the ledger's recorded state can never disagree in
them.

## Problem

`ready_task` must not hand `package_ready_task` an outcome whose
hardcoded `READY_FOR_REVIEW` state disagrees with what today's build's own
selection rule reads off the very `reviews` it just rebuilt. When
`anchored_blockers(reviews)` is non-empty and the task never reached REBUT
(no fresh `rebuttal.json`), the stored `READY_FOR_REVIEW` is not evidence
of anything today's code would still conclude — it is refused by name,
the same way every other staleness `ready_task` already catches is.

A task whose blocker already reached a fresh `rebuttal.json` is not this
case: a fresh REBUT answering it, under whatever rule ran it, is exactly
what let that cell reach `READY_FOR_REVIEW`. It still rebuilds as a
`ReadyTask`.

## Out of scope

- **`run_task`'s own live path.** It hands `package()` the `CellOutcome`
  `run_one_cell` returns directly, computed through `review_state`
  already, never through `ready_task`'s rebuild. Nothing here changes it,
  and `saffron/cli.py`, `saffron/batch.py` and `saffron/regate.py`, every
  other caller of that path, are forbidden.
- **Re-deriving `state` itself.** The fix refuses the mismatch; it does
  not try to compute what `review_state` would have said and ship that
  instead. `package()` still receives the ledger's own
  `"READY_FOR_REVIEW"`, now only when nothing today's build reads off
  `reviews` disagrees with it.
- **The rule that grew the mismatch.** `anchored_blockers`,
  `review_state`, `_disagreements` and `rebut.py`'s own docstrings are
  SA-0299's. Nothing here changes `saffron/phases/review.py`,
  `saffron/phases/rebut.py` or `saffron/report/pr_body.py`.
- **A task whose lens errored.** `review_state` treats an errored lens as
  a stop separately from any blocker count. The ledger never records
  `READY_FOR_REVIEW` for one regardless of build, so `ready_task`'s
  existing checks already cover it; this fix adds no second check for it.

## Notes for the agent

**The one change.** In `ready_task`, right after `rebut_result` is built
(`saffron/task.py:976`), add the refusal: when `rebut_result is None` and
`anchored_blockers(reviews)` is non-empty, return `Refused` naming the
task id and the blocker count, before `wrong_versions`, `notes` or the
`tree_base` pusher lookup run. `anchored_blockers` is already imported at
`saffron/task.py:79`; add no other import. Extend `ready_task`'s own
docstring (`saffron/task.py:897-903`) with one clause naming this cause,
beside the ones it already names.

**The witness, in `tests/test_session.py`.** Write it after
`test_a_survivor_outside_the_diff_still_reaches_rebut`
(`tests/test_session.py:11990`). `ready_task`'s own direct tests live in
`tests/test_task.py`, forbidden here; import its fixture helpers instead
of rebuilding them — `_rt_ledger`, `_rt_task`, `_rt_write_patch` and
`_rt_set_mtime` (`tests/test_task.py:2467,2475,2526,2543`) are plain
functions, not private to the module, and reading them is not editing
that file. `_rt_seed_records` writes an empty `findings.json`; write this
test's own `findings.json` by hand instead, through
`review.LensReview(...).as_dict()` (`review` is already imported at
`tests/test_session.py:41`) with one `adequacy` finding whose `claim`
starts with `review.HOST_FILED`, `severity="blocker"`, `anchored=False`.
Drive three task ids under one ledger: one with that finding and no
`rebuttal.json` (expect `Refused`, naming the blocker count and REBUT),
one with an empty `findings.json` and no `rebuttal.json` (expect
`ReadyTask`), and one with that same finding alongside a hand-written
`rebuttal.json` whose shape `_rebuild_rebut_result`
(`saffron/task.py:859-886`) parses (expect `ReadyTask`). Give every file a
task directory's own uniform mtime at or after `baseline.json`'s, the way
`_rt_seed_records` does, so none reads as another cell's.

**Measured on a prototype over `52bad63b`.** The whole change came to 374
changed tokens by the `size` gate's own counter (`saffron/gates/core/size.py`),
against the `bug` ceiling of 1300 — 29%. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`
and `uv run ty check` passed on the final cut. The witness failed with the
source reverted, failed again under the mutant above, and failed under
each wrong version, each applied as an edit in place of the fix. The full
`tests/test_session.py`, `tests/test_task.py` and `tests/test_cli.py`
suites passed unchanged.

Commit after the witness passes. Uncommitted work dies with the cell.
